pr_title: loop devices: use two file descriptors
pr_body:
Avoid unaligned reads from probes by using two file descriptor for loop
devices: one for dissecting and another (possibly same as first) for block
device use.

Closes: #21176
pr_comments: #21233 is a much simpler fix. PTAL.

issue_context.title: pid1: memory not aligned enough used for reading RootImages with O_DIRECT
issue_context.body:
**systemd version the issue has been seen with**
 > main, bisected to e8c7c4d9d145e0ab1ca75457390fcc698c7e55af onwards

<!-- **NOTE:** Do not submit bug reports about anything but the two most recently released *major* systemd versions upstream! -->
<!--           If there have been multiple stable releases for that major version, please consider updating to a recent one before reporting an issue. -->

<!-- For older version please use distribution trackers (see https://systemd.io/CONTRIBUTING#filing-issues). -->

**Used distribution**
 > Debian

**Linux kernel version used** (`uname -a`)
<!-- Make sure to enclose the pasted kernel version in `backticks`, so that
     GitHub doesn't convert the `#` character typically included in it into a
     reference to old GitHub issues. -->
 > `5.14.0-3`

**CPU architecture issue was seen on**
 > x86_64

**Expected behaviour you didn't see**
 > Mounting a squashfs image as `RootImage=` is successful

**Unexpected behaviour you saw**
Starting a service fails:
```
Oct 29 00:08:06 systemd[15228]: systemd-networkd.service: Failed to set up mount namespacing: Invalid argument
Oct 29 00:08:06 systemd[15228]: systemd-networkd.service: Failed at step NAMESPACE spawning /lib/systemd/systemd-networkd: Invalid argument
Oct 29 00:08:06 systemd[1]: systemd-networkd.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=226/NAMESPACE
Oct 29 00:08:06 systemd[1]: systemd-networkd.service: Failed with result 'exit-code'.
Oct 29 00:08:06 systemd[1]: Failed to start Network Configuration.
Oct 29 00:08:06 systemd[1]: systemd-networkd.service: Scheduled restart job, restart counter is at 5.
Oct 29 00:08:06 systemd[1]: Stopped Network Configuration.
```

**Steps to reproduce the problem**
 > …

**Additional program output to the terminal or log subsystem illustrating the issue**

<!-- Please paste relevant program terminal or journal output here, ideally
     when generated in debug mode (try setting the SYSTEMD_LOG_LEVEL=debug
     environment variable). For very long copy/pasted data consider using a
     service like https://gist.github.com/. Where copy/paste is not possible
     (for example early boot or late shutdown), a photo of the screen might do
     too, but text is always much preferred. -->
Excerpt of strace of PID1 failing when starting `systemd-networkd`:
```text
fstat(4, {st_mode=S_IFBLK|0660, st_rdev=makedev(0xfe, 0x18), ...}) = 0
ioctl(4, BLKGETSIZE64, [54525952])      = 0
openat(AT_FDCWD, "/sys/dev/block/254:24", O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC) = 3
openat(3, "dm/uuid", O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC) = 5
read(5, "LVM-Yugg1eSiCXG0Mruly3MMsgzRGcDsAw8ilggPJxLdtTuHkJAuwSaP2e151VbHpK56\n", 8191) = 69
read(5, "", 8122)                       = 0
close(5)                                = 0
close(3)                                = 0
lseek(4, 54460416, SEEK_SET)            = 54460416
read(4, 0x555f96eaa268, 64)             = -1 EINVAL (Invalid argument)
fsync(4)                                = 0
close(4)                                = 0
openat(AT_FDCWD, "/dev/kmsg", O_WRONLY|O_NOCTTY|O_CLOEXEC) = 3
clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, {tv_sec=36, tv_nsec=197939784}) = 0
writev(3, [{iov_base="<27>", iov_len=4}, {iov_base="systemd", iov_len=7}, {iov_base="[1686]: ", iov_len=8}, {iov_base="systemd-networkd.service: Failed to set up mount namespacing: Invalid argument", iov_len=78}, {iov_base="\n", iov_len=1}], 5) = 98
```
Line
```text
read(4, 0x555f96eaa268, 64)             = -1 EINVAL (Invalid argument)
```
is the problem. Man read(2):

EINVAL fd is attached to an object which is unsuitable for reading; _or the file was opened with the O_DIRECT flag, and either the address specified in buf, the value specified in count, or the file offset is not suitably aligned._

Offset 54460416 (or 0x33f0000) is well aligned and also count 64 looks good to me, so I think the address 0x555f96eaa268 should be more strictly aligned than by 8. Sadly the manual page doesn't tell what exactly is 'suitably aligned'.

I suppose the fix is that `dissect_image()` (or something related) should use `posix_memalign()` to allocate more aligned memory for reading images opened with O_DIRECT. I couldn't locate where the read happens and e8c7c4d9d145e0ab1ca75457390fcc698c7e55af only enables O_DIRECT so it doesn't provide a clue.

The images are raw squashfs without any MBR/GPT partition tables.
comments:
Man [open(2)](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/open.2.html) tells that the alignment restriction could be 512 typically.
```
   O_DIRECT
       The O_DIRECT flag may impose alignment restrictions on the length
       and address of user-space buffers and the file offset of I/Os.
       In Linux alignment restrictions vary by filesystem and kernel
       version and might be absent entirely.  However there is currently
       no filesystem-independent interface for an application to
       discover these restrictions for a given file or filesystem.  Some
       filesystems provide their own interfaces for doing so, for
       example the XFS_IOC_DIOINFO operation in xfsctl(3).

       Under Linux 2.4, transfer sizes, the alignment of the user
       buffer, and the file offset must all be multiples of the logical
       block size of the filesystem.  Since Linux 2.6.0, alignment to
       the logical block size of the underlying storage (typically 512
       bytes) suffices.  The logical block size can be determined using
       the ioctl(2) BLKSSZGET operation or from the shell using the
       command:

           blockdev --getss
```

On my system, `blockdev --getss` for all my squashfs images returns 512, like the underlying block device. I don't know what would happen with a block device formatted with 4k blocks.

Another solution could be to enable O_DIRECT only after probing but sadly this doesn't seem possible with `fcntl()`.
We shouldn't use libblkid on the O_DIRECT fd. Either use it on the resulting block fd, or maintain a separate non-O_DIRECT fd to the image

Hmm, wait. So you are saying that libblkid fails on the block device set up this way? That would be a bug in libblkid. i.e. if we pass an `S_IFBLK` fd to libblkid and it reads data off it thta is not aligned in position and size then this would be a bug in libblkid.

(I initially thought you are saying we pass the `S_IFREG` fd that is what the loopback device is based on to libblkid where it then fails.)
Any chance you can upload a disk image that fails like this somewhere so that i can have a closer look?

> Any chance you can upload a disk image that fails like this somewhere so that i can have a closer look?

@poettering I sent you a small image via email.

In my case it's S_IFBLK:
```
openat(AT_FDCWD, "/dev/levy/acpid-all.squashfs", O_RDONLY|O_NOCTTY|O_NONBLOCK|O_DIRECT|O_CLOEXEC) = 3
fstat(3, {st_mode=S_IFBLK|0660, st_rdev=makedev(0xfe, 0xd), ...}) = 0
ioctl(3, LOOP_GET_STATUS64, 0x418be4ec0b98) = -1 ENOTTY (Inappropriate ioctl for device)
fcntl(3, F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC, 3)            = 4
ioctl(4, _IOC(_IOC_READ, 0x12, 0x80, 0x8), 0x418be4ec0890) = -1 ENOTTY (Inappropriate ioctl for device)
close(3)                                = 0
fstat(4, {st_mode=S_IFBLK|0660, st_rdev=makedev(0xfe, 0xd), ...}) = 0
[clip]
lseek(4, 12517376, SEEK_SET)            = 12517376
read(4, 0x7b91e668f1a8, 64)             = -1 EINVAL (Invalid argument)
```

So do I get this right: you already have a block device? I am confused? What kind of block device is this? I really don't follow anymore...

usually we operate on regular files which we turn into block devices via the loopback layer. But that's not what you are doing here, do I get this right?

The images are stored in LVM logical volume 'levy', so the block device (for example `/dev/levy/acpid-all.squashfs`) is from device-mapper (0xfe, 0xd in the last strace).

The bug indeed doesn't seem to appear for images stored somewhere in the file system, the image doesn't seem to be probed in that case. I use that model only for a few very early services like DM and LVM, the other service images are stored in LVM.

review_comments:
Our coding style says:
> Do not mix function invocations with variable definitions in one line.

Please do
```
_cleanup_close_ int copy = -1, copy_dissect_fd = -1;
...
copy_dissect_fd = loop_device_fd_dup_for_dissect(copy);
```
BTW, I am not familiar with the difference, but is this possible to use `fd_reopen()`?
`dissect_fd` may be leaked when `new()` below fails.
